title: Duration control reduced the count link with later quiet time in 2009-2026 Cascadia tremor episodes with at least 100 detections
abstract: We tested whether episode duration removes the link between tremor count and later quiet time in Cascadia. We reused a published PNSN episode table and checked it against 791,720 raw detections. The primary sample has 1,310 complete episodes with at least 100 detections in 26 bins of 50 km. Duration control lowered the time-controlled pooled rank correlation from 0.275 to 0.147. The paired reduction was 0.127, with a 95% two-year calendar-block interval of 0.037 to 0.198. The remaining later link had an interval of 0.068 to 0.255. The conditional after-minus-before contrast was 0.134, with an interval of -0.001 to 0.325. Thus the later count link remains, but its time-direction contrast is uncertain after duration control. Count-threshold, active-day, and post-2017 checks gave positive later point estimates. This is a conditional catalog association, not proof of stress release, a causal duration effect, or forecast skill. Changing detection, fixed episode rules, shared regional events and block assumptions limit the result. Code, episode data, all bootstrap draws, source hashes, raw and numerical checks, and a figure are included.
